articles.title: Indonesian foragers may have sucked on mind-altering nuts 25,000 years ago, research finds
articles.description: Analysis of two skeletons reveals tooth wear and traces of psychoactive substance in what may be earliest known evidence for human drug taking What may be the earliest known evidence for human drug taking has been traced to ancient Indonesian foragers who sucked on mind-altering nuts as long as 25,000 years ago. Analysis of two exceptionally rare skeletons from the Indonesian island of Sulawesi revealed dramatic tooth wear and traces of a psychoactive substance in the individuals’ remaining teeth, suggesting they routinely sucked on hard, abrasive betel nuts. Continue reading...

articles.title: One giant step: first known adult T rex footprints found in North Dakota
articles.description: The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists. The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK. articles.title: Weatherwatch: soil moisture deficit – how dry are the UK’s thirsty soils?
articles.description: SMD is the moisture the soil must make up until it is at capacity, with very dry conditions over most of England and Wales When the ground is thoroughly wet, after excess rainwater has run off it is said to be at field capacity. Meteorologists describe drought in terms of soil moisture deficit (SMD) from field capacity. The SMD is a measure of how thirsty the soil is, expressed as how many millimetres of rain it would take to top it up to field capacity. In southern England, the SMD tends to hover around zero in winter when fields are wet. In summer it may be about 100mm, going up to 150mm or more in a dry year. The extreme of dryness, when soil has no water accessible to plants, is known as the permanent wilting point or PWP. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘One of the biggest discoveries in science’: have scientists found dark matter? – podcast

source.name: Presented by Madeleine Finlay, with Ian Sample, produced by Joshan Chana, sound design by Joel Cox, the executive producer was Ellie Bury

articles.description: For decades physicists have been puzzling over the enigma of dark matter. articles.title: Drinking very hot drinks could triple risk of oesophageal cancer, study finds
articles.description: Research finds temperature and amount of hot drinks consumed heightens possibility of developing disease Drinking very hot tea and coffee triples the risk of developing cancer of the gullet, the world’s largest study of the link between them has found. articles.title: Indonesian foragers may have sucked on mind-altering nuts 25,000 years ago, research finds

articles.title: One giant step: first known adult T rex footprints found in North Dakota
articles.description: The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists. The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK. Continue reading...

articles.title: Weatherwatch: soil moisture deficit – how dry are the UK’s thirsty soils?
articles.description: SMD is the moisture the soil must make up until it is at capacity, with very dry conditions over most of England and Wales When the ground is thoroughly wet, after excess rainwater has run off it is said to be at field capacity. Meteorologists describe drought in terms of soil moisture deficit (SMD) from field capacity. The SMD is a measure of how thirsty the soil is, expressed as how many millimetres of rain it would take to top it up to field capacity. In southern England, the SMD tends to hover around zero in winter when fields are wet. In summer it may be about 100mm, going up to 150mm or more in a dry year. The extreme of dryness, when soil has no water accessible to plants, is known as the permanent wilting point or PWP. Continue reading...

articles.title: England in better place than start of summer - Root
articles.description: Captain Joe Root says England are in a better place at the end of their tumultuous summer and is impressed by how they have handled the chaos.

articles.title: Norris takes Madrid pole with 'gorgeous' lap
articles.description: Lando Norris takes a superb pole position for McLaren at the Spanish Grand Prix, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

articles.title: 'Celebrations cut short!' - no-ball saves Root after being bowled

articles.title: Osborne makes history as first female jockey to win British Classic
articles.description: Saffie Osborne becomes the first female jockey to win a British Classic Flat race, claiming victory in the St Leger on Highwayman.

articles.title: England's second-half response crushes Australia
articles.description: England produce dominant second-half performance to comfortably defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.

articles.title: Ingebrigtsen withdraws from 1500m showdown with Kerr
articles.description: Jakob Ingebrigtsen will not contest the men's 1500m final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship, putting his reunion with rival Josh Kerr on hold.

articles.title: Root and Cox to the rescue as England beat Pakistan in third Test
articles.description: Captain Joe Root and Jordan Cox help England fight back from an early scare as the hosts recover from 2-2, to successfully chase down 130 and wrap up an eight-wicket win and a 3-0 series clean sweep against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

articles.title: 'Celebrations cut short!' - no-ball saves Root after being bowled
articles.description: England captain Joe Root gets a huge let-off after being bowled for 23 by Mohammed Ali, but the dismissal is overturned after the delivery was a no-ball, with England 35-2, chasing 130 to win the third and final Test at Edgbaston.

articles.title: 'What a start!' - England lose Duckett and Gay in first over
articles.description: England get off to a dreadful start on day four of the final Test as Muhammad Abbas removes Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay in the first over, to leave the home side 2-2, chasing 130 to win at Edgbaston.

articles.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down
articles.description: Amodei's call comes amid growing concerns that AI models may become able to inflict serious damage worldwide.

articles.title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?
articles.description: The BBC's Tom Gerken plays the hotly anticipated superhero game from Spider-Man makers Insomniac.

articles.title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI
articles.description: The Cabinet Office, which leads on AI safety, says the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".

articles.title: Does this AI comic make you laugh?
articles.description: Comedian Garrett Millerick has created an AI avatar based on his own material. Is it any good?

articles.title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
articles.description: The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity.

articles.title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?
articles.description: Europe has some promising battery tech, but can it make up ground lost to Chinese battery giants?

articles.title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog
articles.description: The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon tells the BBC.

articles.title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe
articles.description: The US tech giant says the €13bn data centre project will create tens of thousands of jobs.
